title: Early Voting Begins in New York, New Jersey Elections - ABC7 New York
text:
Early Voting Begins in New York, New Jersey Elections - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut POLITICS 
 Early voting opens today in New York and New Jersey 
 Early voting starts in New York and New Jersey today. The candidates for New York Governor both hit the streets to make their cases to New Yorkers yesterday. Eyewitness News report Saturday, October 24, 2026 11:31AM Share NEW YORK (WABC) -- Early voting began Saturday in New York and New Jersey, giving voters across the tri-state area an opportunity to cast ballots ahead of Election Day.
 Both candidates in New York's gubernatorial race spent Friday campaigning in New York City as the early voting period got underway. Gov. Kathy Hochul and her Republican opponent, Bruce Blakeman, made their cases to voters across the five boroughs.
 Mayor Zohran Mamdani was expected to cast his ballot at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, one of several polling locations in New York City. Early voting will continue for more than a week, allowing voters in New York and New Jersey to avoid the Election Day rush.
 Hochul entered the early voting period with a significant lead in public polling and has sought to strengthen support in New York City. Blakeman, meanwhile, has worked to gain support in the city, a traditional Democratic stronghold, while criticizing Hochul's relationship with Mamdani.
 "And what you're seeing are two individuals who know what our job is to get out there and talk to the people, listen to their concerns directly, roll up our sleeves and deliver for the people," Hochul said.
 "She has been a partner, not just for me, but a partner for the entire city," Mamdani said.
 "You are the most divisive mayor we've ever had. You're pitting one side against the other. You're running the high net worth individuals out of our state to create jobs and economic prosperity," Blakeman said.
 Early voting has already begun in Connecticut. In New York City, polling locations are open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday, Sunday and Monday, with hours changing later in the week.
 Voters in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut can cast ballots before Election Day as campaigns make their final appeals to residents across the region.
